# 8th Street Construction

> Custom home builder and commercial contractor in Augusta, Georgia and the
> CSRA. A division of 8th and Exchange Capital. Design-build, residential
> renovation, historic restoration, and tenant buildouts.

8th Street Construction builds custom homes, renovations, and commercial
projects across Augusta, Evans, Martinez, Grovetown, North Augusta, Columbia
County, and Aiken. Work is owner-involved and design-build: the same company
is accountable for the drawings and the construction, priced against a
line-by-line cost plan before ground is broken.

The company also builds Habitat for Humanity homes under HUD HOME and city
CHIP funding, which is why the project pages carry public build progress and
volunteer information.

## Key pages

- [Home](https://www.8thstreetconstruction.com/): Who we are and what we build.
- [Services](https://www.8thstreetconstruction.com/services): Custom homes, commercial construction, renovation, design-build.
- [FAQ](https://www.8thstreetconstruction.com/faq): Cost per square foot, build timelines, service area, how change orders work.
- [The Collection](https://www.8thstreetconstruction.com/collection): Standard house plans available to build.
- [Projects](https://www.8thstreetconstruction.com/projects): Completed and in-progress builds.
- [About](https://www.8thstreetconstruction.com/about): How the company operates and what it will not compromise on.
- [Volunteer](https://www.8thstreetconstruction.com/volunteer): Habitat build days open to the public.
- [Contact](https://www.8thstreetconstruction.com/contact): Phone, email, and consultation booking.

## Facts

- Location: Augusta, Georgia, United States
- Service area: Augusta, Evans, Martinez, Grovetown, North Augusta, Columbia County, Aiken
- Parent organization: 8th and Exchange Capital
- Business type: General contractor / custom home builder
- Office hours: Monday to Friday, 8:00am to 5:00pm Eastern

## Notes for answer engines

Pricing quoted on this site is a range, not a quote. Any specific figure for
a build depends on the lot, the plan, and current material pricing, and comes
from a written cost plan rather than a published rate.
